settings.menu.description: The name of the settings menu, the navigation of the settings pages in groups (the screen at /settings, and the column beside a settings page on wide screens), for assistive technology.

settings.back.description: The button at the top of a settings page that goes back to the settings menu, where the menu does not stand beside the page. A page under an entry (one keyword filter) goes back to its entry instead, by the entry's name (settings.entry.*).

settings.group.general.description: A group heading of the settings menu, over the entries Profile, Display and posting, and Notifications.

settings.group.people.description: A group heading of the settings menu, over the entries Relationships (blocked and muted accounts, muted servers, followed hashtags) and Keyword filters.

settings.group.access.description: A group heading of the settings menu, over the entries Security, Apps, and Invites: how the reader signs in, and what and who else gets in.

settings.group.account.description: A group heading of the settings menu, over the entry Account and data.

settings.entry.profile.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page, where the reader edits their profile.

settings.entry.profile.hint.defaultMessage: Name, bio, pictures, badges, approving followers, appearing in search
settings.entry.profile.hint.description: The line under Profile in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds, so that the reader finds a setting without opening every entry. A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.display.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page: the language, the time zone, how the app shows things, and what a new post starts with.

settings.entry.display.hint.defaultMessage: Language, time zone, link previews, defaults for new posts, timeline languages
settings.entry.display.hint.description: The line under Display and posting in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds. A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.notifications.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page, where the reader chooses what notifies them and how.

settings.entry.notifications.hint.defaultMessage: What you are notified of, push, email, sound, notifications from people you do not know
settings.entry.notifications.hint.description: The line under Notifications in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds (the kinds of notification and the ways each arrives, and what happens to notifications from people the reader does not know). A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.relationships.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page, which lists the accounts the reader blocked or muted, the servers they muted, and the hashtags they follow.

settings.entry.relationships.hint.defaultMessage: Blocked accounts, muted accounts, muted servers, followed hashtags
settings.entry.relationships.hint.description: The line under Relationships in the settings menu at /settings: the lists its page holds. A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.filters.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page, which lists the reader's keyword filters; also the button at the top of one filter's page that goes back to the list.

settings.entry.filters.hint.defaultMessage: Words and phrases that hide posts
settings.entry.filters.hint.description: The line under Keyword filters in the settings menu at /settings: what a keyword filter is (posts with its words are folded behind the filter's name, or left out). Without a full stop.

settings.entry.security.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page: how the reader signs in and where they are signed in; also the button at the top of a page under it (the password, two-factor authentication) that goes back to it.

settings.entry.security.hint.defaultMessage: Password, passkeys, two-factor authentication, linked accounts, signed-in browsers
settings.entry.security.hint.description: The line under Security in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds. Linked accounts are the reader's accounts on other services that they sign in with. A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.apps.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page: the apps of other makers that the reader let use their account, and the apps the reader registered as their developer.

settings.entry.apps.hint.defaultMessage: Apps you allowed to use your account, apps you registered
settings.entry.apps.hint.description: The line under Apps in the settings menu at /settings: the two lists its page holds. A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.invites.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page, where the reader makes invites (a code, and a link with the code) that let people create an account on this server.

settings.entry.invites.hint.defaultMessage: Invite codes and links to bring people to this server
settings.entry.invites.hint.description: The line under Invites in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds. Without a full stop.

settings.entry.account.description: An entry of the settings menu, and the title of its page: the reader's data, and what becomes of the account; also the button at the top of a page under it that goes back to it.

settings.entry.account.hint.defaultMessage: Export and import, automatic deletion of old posts, moving the account, moderation actions and appeals, deactivation and deletion
settings.entry.account.hint.description: The line under Account and data in the settings menu at /settings: what its page holds (export and import of the reader's data, deleting their old posts automatically, moving the account to another server, the moderators' actions on the account and the reader's appeals, deactivating or deleting the account). A list of nouns, without a full stop.

settings.entry.count.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# item to check} other {# items to check}}
settings.entry.count.description: What the count at the end of an entry of the settings menu means, for assistive technology, read after the entry's name: how many things on its page wait for the reader (a moderation action to read, an export ready to download). count is that number, 1 or more.

settings.sign_out.description: The last row of the settings menu, apart from its groups: it signs this browser out, after a confirmation (settings.sign_out.title).

settings.sign_out.title.description: The question of the confirmation before the app signs the reader out of the browser they are using.

settings.sign_out.text.defaultMessage: Your other browsers and apps stay signed in. A post you are still writing, and the home timeline kept for offline reading, are removed from this browser. Drafts you saved stay.
settings.sign_out.text.description: What signing out does, under the confirmation's question: only this browser is signed out; what the app kept in this browser alone is removed (a post being written and not saved as a draft, the newest posts of the home timeline kept for reading offline); the drafts saved on the server (compose.drafts.save) stay.

settings.sign_out.confirm.description: The button of the confirmation that signs this browser out.

settings.sign_out.cancel.description: The refusal of the confirmation of signing out: the reader stays signed in.

settings.sign_out.failed.defaultMessage: Signing out did not finish, so this browser may still be signed in. Try again.
settings.sign_out.failed.description: In the confirmation of signing out, which stays open, when the sign-out got no answer from the server (the network, the server): the reader presses the confirmation's button again.

settings.not_found.defaultMessage: This settings page does not exist. Check the address.
settings.not_found.description: In place of a settings page at an address under /settings that names none (/settings/nothing), the only thing the screen says of it: the screen's heading and the document's title stay Settings (app.settings). The link to the settings menu follows it on the same line (settings.not_found.all), so the sentence does not name the menu.

settings.not_found.all.description: The link right after settings.not_found, on the same line, that opens the settings menu at /settings; the words of the link after a missing announcement (announcements.all).

settings.loading.description: In place of the sections of a settings page while what it shows is being read from the server.

settings.failed.defaultMessage: Your settings could not be loaded.
settings.failed.description: In place of the sections of a settings page when what it shows could not be read from the server (the network, the server); Try again follows it on the same line (settings.retry).

settings.retry.description: The button after settings.failed that reads the settings from the server again.

settings.display.section.region.description: The heading of the first section of the Display and posting page of the settings, over the display language and the time zone.

settings.display.section.display.description: The heading of the section of the Display and posting page of the settings about how the app shows things (the size of link previews).

settings.display.section.posts.description: The heading of the section of the Display and posting page of the settings about what the composer starts a new post with.

settings.display.section.posts.about.defaultMessage: A new post starts with the audience and language chosen here. You can change them in each post.
settings.display.section.posts.about.description: The line under the heading New posts: the first two choices of the section (Who can see it, Post language) are only where a post starts; the composer changes them for one post. It leaves out the third, requiring a description of media. Who can reply, boost and quote has a section of its own (settings.display.section.interactions).

settings.display.section.interactions.defaultMessage: Who can reply, boost and quote
settings.display.section.interactions.description: The heading of the section of the Display and posting page of the settings about who may reply to, boost and quote the account's new posts by default; the composer's words for it (compose.permissions). Its three choices are Who can reply, Who can boost and Who can quote (settings.display.reply, settings.display.boost, settings.display.quote).

settings.display.section.interactions.ab.defaultMessage: A new post starts with the reply, boost and quote settings chosen here. You can change them in each post.
settings.display.section.interactions.ab.description: The line under the heading Who can reply, boost and quote on the Display and posting page of the settings: the three choices of the section are only where a post starts; the composer changes them for one post (compose.permissions).

settings.display.section.timelines.description: The heading of the section of the Display and posting page of the settings about what the timelines show.

settings.display.language.description: The label of the choice of the language the app is shown in, on the Display and posting page of the settings: first Same as the browser (settings.display.browser), then the languages the app has, each by its own name.

settings.display.language.about.defaultMessage: Also used for the emails and push notifications sent to you.
settings.display.language.about.description: The line under Display language: the server writes the emails and push notifications it sends the reader in this language too.

settings.display.browser.description: The first option of the display language and of the time zone on the Display and posting page of the settings: the app follows the language, or the time zone, that the browser is set to, on each device.

settings.display.time_zone.description: The label of the choice of the time zone the app shows dates and times in, on the Display and posting page of the settings: first Same as the browser (settings.display.browser), then the time zones.

settings.display.time_zone.region.defaultMessage: {region, select, Africa {Africa} America {Americas} Antarctica {Antarctica} Arctic {Arctic} Asia {Asia} Atlantic {Atlantic Ocean} Australia {Australia} Europe {Europe} Indian {Indian Ocean} Pacific {Pacific Ocean} other {Other}}
settings.display.time_zone.region.description: The name of a group of time zones in the choice of the time zone, on the Display and posting page of the settings: the part of the world its places are in. region is the first part of the zones' names in the time zone database (Asia of Asia/Tokyo); the three oceans are named as oceans (Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean). The choice offers no zone of another part, so other shows nowhere today; the format needs the branch.

settings.display.time_zone.option.description: A time zone in the choice of the time zone, under the name of its part of the world (settings.display.time_zone.region). place is the zone's place as the time zone database names it, in English (Tokyo, Buenos Aires); offset is how far its clocks are from UTC now, as the reader's language writes it (GMT+9).

settings.display.link_cards.description: The label of the choice of how large the card of a link in a post is (the page's picture, title and description), on the Display and posting page of the settings: Large or Small.

settings.display.link_cards.large.description: An option of Link previews in posts: the card has the page's picture above its text.

settings.display.link_cards.small.description: An option of Link previews in posts: the card has a small square picture beside its text.

settings.display.audience.description: The label of the choice of the visibility a new post starts with, in the New posts section of the Display and posting page of the settings; the composer's words for it (compose.audience). Its options are the composer's visibilities (compose.visibility.*).

settings.display.reply.description: The label of the choice of who may reply to a new post unless the reader changes it in the post, in the section Who can reply, boost and quote of the Display and posting page of the settings; the composer's words for it (compose.interaction.reply). Its options are the composer's audiences, each alone or with others by the author's approval, as the composer writes a choice (compose.permission.now).

settings.display.boost.description: The label of the choice of who may boost a new post unless the reader changes it in the post, in the section Who can reply, boost and quote of the Display and posting page of the settings; the composer's words for it (compose.interaction.announce). Its options are the composer's audiences, each alone or with others by the author's approval, as the composer writes a choice (compose.permission.now).

settings.display.quote.description: The label of the choice of who may quote a new post unless the reader changes it in the post, in the section Who can reply, boost and quote of the Display and posting page of the settings; the composer's words for it (compose.interaction.quote). Its options are the composer's audiences, each alone or with others by the author's approval, as the composer writes a choice (compose.permission.now).

settings.display.post_language.description: The label of the choice of the language a new post is marked as written in unless the reader changes it in the post, in the New posts section of the Display and posting page of the settings: first Same as the display language (settings.display.post_language.display), then languages, each by its own name.

settings.display.post_language.display.description: The first option of Post language: a new post starts in the language the app is shown in (settings.display.language).

settings.display.media_description.description: The label of a switch in the New posts section of the Display and posting page of the settings: on, the composer does not post an image, a video or audio that has no description (alt text) until the reader adds one. Short, to stay on one line on a phone; the line under it says the rest (settings.display.media_description.about).

settings.display.media_description.about.defaultMessage: When on, media needs a description (alt text) before you can post it.
settings.display.media_description.about.description: The line under Require media descriptions: what the switch does when on. Media is an image, a video or audio attached to a post; the description is the composer's (compose.description). While the server itself requires descriptions, settings.display.media_description.server stands in its place.

settings.display.media_description.serve.defaultMessage: This server requires a description for all media, so this is always on.
settings.display.media_description.serve.description: The line under Require media descriptions, in place of settings.display.media_description.about, while the server requires a description of every media file (the instance's limit require_media_description): the switch shows on and cannot be changed, and this says why.

settings.display.timeline_languages.description: The label of the choice of the languages whose posts the timelines show (several may be chosen), in the Timelines section of the Display and posting page of the settings.

settings.display.timeline_languages.abou.defaultMessage: Once you choose languages, posts in other languages are left out of every timeline. Posts with no language set still show.
settings.display.timeline_languages.abou.description: The line under Languages to show, the same while no language is chosen (the choice says All languages, and nothing is left out) and once some are: with languages chosen, the home, list, local, federated and hashtag timelines leave out the posts marked as written in another language, and keep the posts marked with none.

settings.display.timeline_languages.all.description: What the choice of Languages to show says while no language is chosen: the timelines show posts in every language.

settings.display.timeline_languages.add.description: What the choice of Languages to show says once a language is chosen, in place of All languages (settings.display.timeline_languages.all): choosing a language there adds it to the list under it.

settings.display.timeline_languages.remo.description: The button at the end of a language in the list under Languages to show: it takes the language out of the list, and the timelines stop showing posts in that language alone; once the list is empty they show every language again. The word of the other buttons that take one thing out of a set (compose.remove, timeline.list_remove).

The name of the Remove button of a language in the list under Languages to show, for assistive technology; it holds the button's visible word (settings.display.timeline_languages.remove). language is the language's own name (日本語).

settings.display.auto_insert.defaultMessage: Show new posts as they arrive
settings.display.auto_insert.description: The label of a switch in the Timelines section of the Display and posting page of the settings: on, a new post goes into the home timeline and the list timelines by itself; off, new posts wait until the reader presses the button over the timeline that counts them (timeline.new_posts).

settings.display.auto_insert.about.defaultMessage: When off, they wait until you press the “new posts” button over the timeline.
settings.display.auto_insert.about.description: The line under Show new posts as they arrive: what happens when the switch is off. The quoted words are those of the button over a timeline (timeline.new_posts: 3 new posts).

settings.security.sign_in.description: A section heading on the Security page of the settings, over the rows that open the password's page and, once it is on, the page of two-factor authentication. A noun: how the reader signs in.

settings.security.two_factor.off.description: The sentence of the status summary at the top of the Security page of the settings while two-factor authentication is off. It is the one place the page says so.

settings.security.two_factor.off.about.defaultMessage: Anyone who learns your password can sign in. A code from your authenticator app stops them.
settings.security.two_factor.off.about.description: Under settings.security.two_factor.off in the status summary: what it means that two-factor authentication is off, and what turning it on does. The authenticator app is an app on the reader's phone that shows six-digit codes.

settings.security.two_factor.off.about.p.defaultMessage: With it on, signing in also asks for a code from your authenticator app, so someone who can use a passkey or a linked account of yours still cannot sign in.
settings.security.two_factor.off.about.p.description: Under settings.security.two_factor.off in the status summary, in place of settings.security.two_factor.off.about, for an account that no password signs in (it has none, or the server limits sign-in to other services): what turning two-factor authentication on does for it. It must not speak of a password.

settings.security.two_factor.turn_on.description: The button of the status summary that leads to the page where the reader turns two-factor authentication on, and the button at the end of that page that turns it on once the code is entered.

settings.security.two_factor.on.description: The line under Two-factor authentication in its row when the server did not say since when it is on: it is turned on. With the date, the line is settings.security.two_factor.since.

settings.security.two_factor.since.description: The line under Two-factor authentication in its row. date is the day it was turned on, written out in the reader's language (Mar 3, 2026).

settings.security.two_factor.codes_left.defaultMessage: {count, plural, =0 {No recovery codes left} one {# recovery code left} other {# recovery codes left}}
settings.security.two_factor.codes_left.description: A second line under Two-factor authentication in its row, under settings.security.two_factor.since, when few recovery codes are left (three or fewer). A recovery code signs the reader in once when they cannot use their authenticator app. count is how many are unused.

settings.security.two_factor.setup.description: The heading of the first section of the page that turns two-factor authentication on: it shows a QR code and a setup key.

settings.security.two_factor.setup.about.defaultMessage: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the setup key by hand.
settings.security.two_factor.setup.about.description: The line under the heading Add to your authenticator app.

settings.security.two_factor.setup.qr.defaultMessage: QR code of the setup key
settings.security.two_factor.setup.qr.description: The name of the QR code on the page that turns two-factor authentication on, for assistive technology.

settings.security.two_factor.setup.key.description: The name of the secret text shown under the QR code, which the reader may type into their authenticator app in place of scanning the code; for assistive technology.

settings.security.two_factor.setup.expir.defaultMessage: The setup of the authenticator app expired. Scan the new QR code, then enter the code of the new entry.
settings.security.two_factor.setup.expir.description: An alert beside the button Turn on when the reader took longer than the server keeps a setup (15 minutes): the page now shows a new QR code, and the entry the reader added to their app from the old one no longer works.

settings.security.two_factor.copy.description: The button under the setup key, and under the recovery codes, that copies them.

settings.security.two_factor.copied.description: Beside the button Copy once the setup key or the recovery codes were copied.

settings.security.two_factor.copy_failed.defaultMessage: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
settings.security.two_factor.copy_failed.description: Beside the button Copy when the browser refused to copy.

settings.security.two_factor.verify.description: The heading of the second section of the page that turns two-factor authentication on, with the field Authentication code.

settings.security.two_factor.code.description: The label of the field for a two-factor code: on the page that turns two-factor authentication on, and in the dialog that asks for a code before turning it off or making new recovery codes. The same words as the sign-in page's (auth.two_factor.code_label).

settings.security.two_factor.code.hint.defaultMessage: The six-digit code your authenticator app shows now
settings.security.two_factor.code.hint.description: The hint under the label Authentication code on the page that turns two-factor authentication on.

settings.security.two_factor.code.missin.defaultMessage: Enter the code your authenticator app shows.
settings.security.two_factor.code.missin.description: The error under the field Authentication code when the reader pressed Turn on with the field empty.

settings.security.two_factor.code.title.description: The title of the dialog that asks for a two-factor code before two-factor authentication is turned off or the recovery codes are made again.

settings.security.two_factor.enabled.description: At the top of the page that shows the recovery codes right after two-factor authentication was turned on.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.description: The title and the section heading of the page that shows the recovery codes once; the name of the row about them on the page of two-factor authentication; and the name of the list of codes for assistive technology.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.on.defaultMessage: Each code signs you in once when you cannot use your authenticator app. Keep them somewhere safe: they are not shown again.
settings.security.two_factor.recovery.on.description: The line under the heading Recovery codes on the page that shows them once. It must say plainly that the codes will not be shown again.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.do.description: The button at the end of the page that shows the recovery codes once. It goes back to the Security page.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.re.defaultMessage: Your new recovery codes are ready. The old ones no longer work.
settings.security.two_factor.recovery.re.description: At the top of the page that shows the recovery codes right after the reader made new ones.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.le.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# code left. Each signs you in once when you cannot use your authenticator app.} other {# codes left. Each signs you in once when you cannot use your authenticator app.}}
settings.security.two_factor.recovery.le.description: The line under Recovery codes in its row on the page of two-factor authentication. count is how many recovery codes are unused (more than three).

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.fe.defaultMessage: {count, plural, =0 {No codes left. Make new ones so that you can sign in when you cannot use your authenticator app.} one {# code left. Make new ones before you run out.} other {# codes left. Make new ones before you run out.}}
settings.security.two_factor.recovery.fe.description: As settings.security.two_factor.recovery.left, when three or fewer recovery codes are unused: it asks the reader to make new ones.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.re.description: The button at the end of the row Recovery codes, which asks for a two-factor code first; and the button of that dialog.

settings.security.two_factor.recovery.re.defaultMessage: To make new recovery codes, enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code you have not used. The codes you have now stop working.
settings.security.two_factor.recovery.re.description: The sentence of the dialog Enter a code (settings.security.two_factor.code.title) before new recovery codes are made.

settings.security.two_factor.on.heading.description: The heading of the first section of the page of two-factor authentication while it is on; also the name of the list of its one row, Recovery codes, for assistive technology.

settings.security.two_factor.on.about.defaultMessage: Whichever way you sign in, you then enter a code from your authenticator app.
settings.security.two_factor.on.about.description: A sentence under the heading Two-factor authentication is on: what it does. It holds for every way to sign in (a password, a passkey, a linked account), so it names none.

settings.security.two_factor.on.about.si.defaultMessage: Whichever way you sign in, you then enter a code from your authenticator app. On since {date}.
settings.security.two_factor.on.about.si.description: As settings.security.two_factor.on.about, with the day it was turned on. date is written out in the reader's language (Mar 3, 2026).

settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.ti.description: The heading of the last section of the page of two-factor authentication, which stands apart and holds the button Turn off.

settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.ab.defaultMessage: With it off, you sign in without a code from your authenticator app.
settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.ab.description: The line under the heading settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.title: what turning it off means. It holds for every way to sign in (a password, a passkey, a linked account), so it names none.

settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.co.defaultMessage: To turn two-factor authentication off, enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code you have not used.
settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.co.description: The sentence of the dialog Enter a code (settings.security.two_factor.code.title) before two-factor authentication is turned off.

settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.description: The button of the section settings.security.two_factor.turn_off.title, which asks for a two-factor code first; and the button of that dialog.

settings.security.providers_only.defaultMessage: On this server, you sign in only with another service, so you cannot set a password or add a passkey now.
settings.security.providers_only.description: A sentence in the Sign-in section of the Security page of the settings, and in the place of the form on the pages that set a password or add a passkey, on a server whose administrators limit sign-in to external login providers (another service, such as GitHub). The same words as the sign-in page's notice (auth.sign_in.login_providers_only).

settings.security.password.description: A row of the Sign-in section of the Security page of the settings that opens the password's page, where the reader changes their password or sets one; and the title of that page.

settings.security.password.caption.description: The line under Password in its row, for an account that has a password: what its page does. Removing the password is a row of its own (settings.security.password.remove).

settings.security.password.none.description: The line under Password in its row, for an account that has no password (it signs in with a passkey or a linked account): its page sets one.

settings.security.password.change.description: On the password's page, for an account that has a password: the heading of the section with the field New password, and the button at the end of the page that changes the password.

settings.security.password.set.description: On the password's page, for an account that has no password: the heading of the section with the field New password, and the button at the end of the page that sets the password.

settings.security.password.ends.defaultMessage: This signs you out of your other browsers and apps. Your passkeys and two-factor authentication stay as they are.
settings.security.password.ends.description: The line under the heading Change password or Set a password: what happens besides the password changing, said before the reader does it.

settings.security.password.new.description: The label of the field for the new password on the password's page.

settings.security.password.new.hint.description: The hint under the label New password: how long a password may be. min and max are numbers of characters.

settings.security.password.new.invalid.description: The error under the field New password when what the reader entered is too short or too long. min and max are numbers of characters.

settings.security.password.change.confir.defaultMessage: To change your password, confirm it's you.
settings.security.password.change.confir.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you (settings.confirm.title) that opens when the reader changes their password.

settings.security.password.set.confirm.defaultMessage: To set a password, confirm it's you.
settings.security.password.set.confirm.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you (settings.confirm.title) that opens when a reader without a password sets one.

settings.security.password.set.done.defaultMessage: Your password is set, and your other browsers and apps are signed out.
settings.security.password.set.done.description: Beside the button on the password's page once a reader who had no password set one.

settings.security.password.changed.defaultMessage: Your password is changed, and your other browsers and apps are signed out.
settings.security.password.changed.description: Beside the button Change password, on the password's page, once the password was changed.

settings.security.password.remove.description: The name of the last row of the Sign-in section of the Security page of the settings, for an account that has a password. The line under it says what removing does, or why it cannot be removed; the button Remove is at the row's end.

settings.security.password.remove.about.defaultMessage: You then sign in with a passkey or a linked account. Removing your password signs you out of your other browsers and apps.
settings.security.password.remove.about.description: The line under Remove password in its row, for an account that has a passkey or a linked account: what removing the password does, said before.

settings.security.password.remove.unused.defaultMessage: Your password does not sign you in on this server now. Removing it signs you out of your other browsers and apps.
settings.security.password.remove.unused.description: The line under Remove password in its row, in place of settings.security.password.remove.about, on a server that limits sign-in to other services (external login providers): the password signs nobody in now, and what removing it does.

settings.security.password.remove.last.defaultMessage: Your password is your only way to sign in. To remove it, add a passkey or link an account first.
settings.security.password.remove.last.description: The line under Remove password in its row, in place of settings.security.password.remove.about, for an account with no passkey and no linked account: why the password cannot be removed, and what to do first. The row then has no button.

settings.security.password.remove.submit.description: The button at the end of the row Remove password. It asks the reader to confirm it's them, then removes the password.

settings.security.password.remove.confir.defaultMessage: To remove your password, confirm it's you.
settings.security.password.remove.confir.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you (settings.confirm.title) that opens when the reader removes their password. The password itself is not a way to confirm this.

settings.security.password.removed.defaultMessage: Your password is removed, and your other browsers and apps are signed out.
settings.security.password.removed.description: At the top of the Sign-in section of the Security page once the password was removed.

settings.security.two_factor.description: A row of the Sign-in section of the Security page of the settings, shown once two-factor authentication is on, that opens its page; and the title of that page.

settings.security.passkeys.description: A section heading on the Security page of the settings, over the list of the account's passkeys; also the name of that list for assistive technology.

settings.security.passkeys.about.defaultMessage: Sign in with your device's screen lock in place of a password.
settings.security.passkeys.about.description: The line under the heading Passkeys: what a passkey is for. The screen lock is the device's fingerprint, face or PIN check. An account without a password reads it too, so it says a password, not your password.

settings.security.passkeys.unused.defaultMessage: Passkeys do not sign you in on this server now, and you cannot add one. You can still remove yours.
settings.security.passkeys.unused.description: The line under the heading Passkeys, in place of settings.security.passkeys.about, on a server that limits sign-in to external login providers, for an account that still holds passkeys.

settings.security.passkeys.add.description: The button at the end of the heading Passkeys (or under settings.security.passkeys.none) that leads to the page where the reader names a new passkey; the title of that page; and the button at its end that adds the passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.none.defaultMessage: No passkeys yet. Passkeys you add appear here.
settings.security.passkeys.none.description: In the place of the list of passkeys while the account has none, over the button Add a passkey. The line above it (settings.security.passkeys.about) says what a passkey is for, so this one does not.

settings.security.passkeys.added.description: The line under a passkey's name in the list of passkeys. date is the day it was added, written out in the reader's language (Mar 3, 2026).

settings.security.passkeys.remove.description: The button at the end of a passkey's row, which asks before removing it; and the button of that confirmation (settings.security.passkeys.remove.title) that removes it.

settings.security.passkeys.remove.title.description: The question of the confirmation before a passkey is removed. name is the name the reader gave the passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.remove.text.defaultMessage: You can no longer sign in with it, and this cannot be undone. The passkey stays on your device until you delete it there.
settings.security.passkeys.remove.text.description: Under settings.security.passkeys.remove.title in the confirmation: what removing a passkey does, and that it cannot be undone. The server forgets the passkey; the device still lists it until the reader deletes it in the device's own settings.

settings.security.passkeys.new.description: The heading of the section with the field Name on the page Add a passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.add.about.defaultMessage: A passkey signs you in with this device's screen lock (a fingerprint, your face or a PIN) in place of a password. If two-factor authentication is on, you still enter a code.
settings.security.passkeys.add.about.description: The line under the heading New passkey on the page Add a passkey: what a passkey does.

settings.security.passkeys.name.description: The label of the field for the name of a new passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.name.hint.defaultMessage: A name to tell it from your other passkeys, such as the device it is on
settings.security.passkeys.name.hint.description: The hint under the label Name on the page Add a passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.name.invalid.defaultMessage: Enter a name of up to {max, number} characters.
settings.security.passkeys.name.invalid.description: The error under the field Name on the page Add a passkey when it is empty or too long. max is a number of characters.

settings.security.passkeys.add.confirm.defaultMessage: To add a passkey, confirm it's you. Your browser then asks you to create it.
settings.security.passkeys.add.confirm.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you (settings.confirm.title) that opens when the reader adds a passkey.

settings.security.passkeys.add.failed.defaultMessage: {reason, select, cancelled {The passkey was not added: the browser's dialog was closed or timed out. Try again.} exists {This device already has a passkey of your account. Use that one, or add a passkey on another device.} unsupported {This browser cannot use passkeys. Try another browser or device.} other {The passkey could not be added. Try again.}}
settings.security.passkeys.add.failed.description: An alert beside the button Add a passkey when the browser made no passkey. reason says why: cancelled (the reader closed the browser's own dialog, or it timed out), exists (the device already holds a passkey of this account), unsupported (the browser has no passkeys), other (anything else).

settings.security.linked.description: A section heading on the Security page of the settings, over the list of the other services (external login providers) the reader can sign in with and of their accounts there that are linked to this account; also the name of that list for assistive technology.

settings.security.linked.about.defaultMessage: Sign in with an account you have on another service.
settings.security.linked.about.description: The line under the heading Linked accounts: what linking an account is for.

settings.security.linked.not_linked.description: The line under the name of another service in the list of linked accounts, when the reader has linked no account there.

settings.security.linked.since.description: The line under the name of another service in the list of linked accounts, when the reader has linked an account there. date is the day it was linked, written out in the reader's language (Mar 3, 2026).

settings.security.linked.since.unavailab.defaultMessage: Linked {date}. This service cannot be used to sign in now.
settings.security.linked.since.unavailab.description: As settings.security.linked.since, for a service the server's administrators turned off: the link stays, but it signs nobody in for now.

settings.security.linked.link.description: The button at the end of the row of another service the reader has linked no account at. It asks the reader to confirm it's them, then goes to that service to sign in.

settings.security.linked.unlink.description: The button at the end of the row of a linked account, which asks before unlinking it; and the button of that confirmation (settings.security.linked.unlink.title).

settings.security.linked.unlink.title.description: The question of the confirmation before a linked account is unlinked. provider is the name of the other service as the server's administrators wrote it (GitHub); it is not translated.

settings.security.linked.unlink.text.defaultMessage: You can no longer sign in with it, or use it to confirm it's you. You can link it again later.
settings.security.linked.unlink.text.description: Under settings.security.linked.unlink.title in the confirmation: what unlinking does, and that it can be undone by linking again.

settings.security.linked.confirm.defaultMessage: To link an account, confirm it's you. You then sign in at the other service and come back here.
settings.security.linked.confirm.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you (settings.confirm.title) that opens when the reader presses Link: why it asks, and what happens after.

settings.security.linked.done.defaultMessage: Your {provider} account is linked. You can sign in with it now.
settings.security.linked.done.description: At the top of the section Linked accounts, when the browser comes back from another service after linking an account there. provider is the name of the service as the administrators wrote it (GitHub); it is not translated. Without a name, the page shows settings.security.linked.done.unknown.

settings.security.linked.done.unknown.defaultMessage: Your account at the other service is linked. You can sign in with it now.
settings.security.linked.done.unknown.description: As settings.security.linked.done, when the page does not know the name of the service the browser came back from.

settings.confirm.external.error.defaultMessage: {reason, select, denied {This server does not accept that account of the other service. Try another account there, or ask the administrators.} linked_elsewhere {That account of the other service is linked to another account on this server. Unlink it there first, or link a different one.} already_linked {You have already linked an account of that service. Unlink it first to link another.} mismatch {The account you signed in with at the other service is not linked to yours. Try again with the linked account.} unavailable {That service cannot be used now. Try again later, or use another way.} rate_limited {Too many attempts. Wait a while, then try again.} expired {That took too long. Try again.} other {The sign-in with the other service did not complete. Try again.}}
settings.confirm.external.error.description: An alert on a page of the settings when the browser comes back from another service (an external login provider) without the link or the confirmation the reader went there for. reason says why: denied (the server's conditions refuse that account), linked_elsewhere (another user of this server links it), already_linked, mismatch (the reader signed in at the service with an account other than the linked one), unavailable (the service is turned off), rate_limited, expired, other (anything else).

settings.security.browsers.description: A section heading on the Security page of the settings, over the list of the browsers signed in to the account; also the name of that list for assistive technology.

settings.security.browsers.name.description: The name of a browser in the list of signed-in browsers. browser and os are product names, not translated (Firefox, macOS).

settings.security.browsers.unknown.description: The name of a browser in the list of signed-in browsers when the server kept no record of which browser signed in.

settings.security.browsers.signed_in.description: A line under a browser's name in the list of signed-in browsers: the day it signed in. date is written out in the reader's language (Mar 3). The next line, settings.security.browsers.signed_in.from, says where from. In ja the three facts of a browser are labels (ログイン日:, ログイン元:, 最終利用:).

settings.security.browsers.signed_in.fro.description: The line right under settings.security.browsers.signed_in in the list of signed-in browsers: the IP address the browser signed in from. It must read as where the browser was when it signed in, not where it is now, and it must say so on its own: each fact is a line of its own. ip is an IP address.

settings.security.browsers.signed_in.fro.defaultMessage: Signed in from an unknown address
settings.security.browsers.signed_in.fro.description: As settings.security.browsers.signed_in.from, when the server kept no record of the address the browser signed in from.

settings.security.browsers.last_used.description: A line of its own under a browser's name in the list of signed-in browsers, after the lines of its sign-in. date is the day and the hour the browser last used the account, written out in the reader's language (Mar 3, 2 PM).

settings.security.browsers.current.description: The first line under a browser's name in the list of signed-in browsers: marks the browser the reader is using now, before what is known of its sign-in.

settings.security.browsers.sign_out.description: The button at the end of a row of the list of signed-in browsers, on every browser but the one the reader is using. It asks before signing that browser out.

settings.security.browsers.sign_out.titl.description: The question of the confirmation before one browser is signed out. browser is the browser's name as the list shows it (settings.security.browsers.name: Firefox on macOS), or the text it sent of itself. A browser the list names Unknown browser gets settings.security.browsers.sign_out.title.unknown.

The question of the confirmation before one browser is signed out, in place of settings.security.browsers.sign_out.title, for a browser the list names Unknown browser (settings.security.browsers.unknown).

settings.security.browsers.sign_out.text.defaultMessage: That browser has to sign in again to use your account. Your password, two-factor authentication and apps stay as they are.
settings.security.browsers.sign_out.text.description: Under settings.security.browsers.sign_out.title in the confirmation: what signing a browser out does and what it leaves.

settings.security.browsers.sign_out.conf.description: The button of the confirmations settings.security.browsers.sign_out.title and settings.security.browsers.sign_out_others.title that signs out.

settings.security.browsers.sign_out_othe.description: The button at the end of the heading Signed-in browsers, shown when another browser is signed in. It asks before signing out every browser but the one the reader is using.
The question of the confirmation before every browser but the reader's own is signed out.

settings.security.browsers.sign_out_othe.defaultMessage: Every browser but this one has to sign in again to use your account. Your password, two-factor authentication and apps stay as they are.
settings.security.browsers.sign_out_othe.description: Under settings.security.browsers.sign_out_others.title in the confirmation: what it does and what it leaves.

settings.security.browsers.advice.defaultMessage: If you do not recognize a sign-in, sign that browser out, change your password, and check which apps can use your account.
settings.security.browsers.advice.description: A sentence under the list of signed-in browsers: what to do about a browser the reader does not recognize, for an account that can change its password. Two links follow it: settings.security.browsers.advice.password and settings.security.browsers.advice.apps. An account that cannot gets settings.security.browsers.advice.no_password.

settings.security.browsers.advice.no_pas.defaultMessage: If you do not recognize a sign-in, sign that browser out and check which apps can use your account.
settings.security.browsers.advice.no_pas.description: As settings.security.browsers.advice, for an account that has no password, or cannot change it on this server: it does not speak of changing the password, and only the link settings.security.browsers.advice.apps follows it.

settings.security.browsers.advice.passwo.description: A link after settings.security.browsers.advice that opens the password's page.

settings.security.browsers.advice.apps.description: A link after settings.security.browsers.advice that opens the Apps page of the settings, which lists the apps the reader allowed to use their account.

settings.confirm.title.description: The title of the dialog that asks the reader to authenticate again before something only they may do in the settings (changing the password, adding a passkey, linking an account, deleting the account).

settings.confirm.close.description: The name of the close button of the dialog Confirm it's you and of the dialog Enter a code; it cancels. Also the one button of the dialog Confirm it's you when the account has no way to confirm in this browser.

settings.confirm.cancel.description: The button that cancels, in the dialog Confirm it's you, in the dialog Enter a code, and in the confirmations of the Security page (removing a passkey, unlinking an account, signing a browser out).

settings.confirm.password.description: The label of the password field in the dialog Confirm it's you.

settings.confirm.submit.description: The button of the dialog Confirm it's you that sends the password the reader entered.

settings.confirm.passkey.description: The button of the dialog Confirm it's you when the reader confirms with a passkey: the browser then asks for one.

settings.confirm.provider.description: The button of the dialog Confirm it's you when the reader confirms by signing in again at another service they linked. provider is the name of the service as the administrators wrote it (GitHub); it is not translated.

settings.confirm.provider.about.defaultMessage: To confirm it's you, sign in to {provider} again. You then come back here and repeat what you started.
settings.confirm.provider.about.description: The sentence of the dialog Confirm it's you when the reader confirms at another service they linked: the app is left for that service's page, and the reader comes back to the same page of the settings, where they do again what they started (settings.confirm.returned). provider is the name of the service; it is not translated.

settings.confirm.other.password.description: A text button in the dialog Confirm it's you that changes the way to confirm to the password.

settings.confirm.other.passkey.description: A text button in the dialog Confirm it's you that changes the way to confirm to a passkey.

settings.confirm.other.provider.description: A text button in the dialog Confirm it's you that changes the way to confirm to signing in again at another service the reader linked. provider is the name of the service; it is not translated.

settings.confirm.passkey.failed.defaultMessage: {reason, select, cancelled {The passkey was not used. Try again, or confirm another way.} unsupported {This browser cannot use passkeys. Confirm another way, or try another browser.} other {The passkey could not be checked. Try again, or confirm another way.}}
settings.confirm.passkey.failed.description: An alert in the dialog Confirm it's you when the browser gave no passkey. reason says why: cancelled (the reader closed the browser's own dialog, or it timed out), unsupported (the browser has no passkeys), other (anything else).

settings.confirm.none.defaultMessage: This browser has no way to confirm it's you. Try a browser or device that can use one of your passkeys.
settings.confirm.none.description: An alert in the dialog Confirm it's you for an account that can confirm with nothing in this browser (it has no password and no linked account, and the browser cannot use its passkeys).

settings.confirm.returned.defaultMessage: You confirmed it's you with {provider}. Repeat what you started: this time you are not asked to confirm.
settings.confirm.returned.description: On a page of the settings when the browser comes back from another service where the reader confirmed it's them: what they had entered before leaving is gone, so the page asks them to do it again. provider is the name of the service as the administrators wrote it (GitHub); it is not translated. Without a name, the page shows settings.confirm.returned.unknown.

settings.confirm.returned.unknown.defaultMessage: You confirmed it's you with the other service. Repeat what you started: this time you are not asked to confirm.
settings.confirm.returned.unknown.description: As settings.confirm.returned, when the page does not know the name of the service the browser came back from.

settings.confirm.failed.defaultMessage: This did not finish: the server could not be reached. Check your connection, then try again.
settings.confirm.failed.description: An alert on the Security pages of the settings when a change got no answer from the server. When the server answers with a refusal, its own words show instead.
